title: POC queueing & capacity sprint proposal
body:
Purpose / quick summary:
Run a focused 3-week POC to validate queueing and capacity behavior for AcmeCorp's customer support assistant (multitenant, ~10k daily active users, bursty morning traffic). We want to show predictable latency under Dedicated and a compatible private deployment fallback plan. Primary deliverable = capacity model + demo showing stable p95 latency < 350ms for short chats and graceful degradation for long-form generation.

Why this matters (context):
- AcmeCorp is evaluating Dedicated vs Private for regulatory reasons; they care about deterministic latency during support peak windows.
- Our current guidance (optimize batching + KV prefix caching) needs to be stress-tested with realistic arrival patterns and sequence-length mix.
- Sales requires a concrete capacity estimate and an ops playbook for canary-to-production rollouts.

Success metrics (what customer will sign off on):
- p95 token latency for <=128-token responses: < 350ms on Dedicated config proposed
- graceful fallback: when capacity saturated, degraded model (quantized) serves with p95 < 900ms and error rate < 2%
- cost estimate within 15% of modeled projection for steady-state month
- handoff artifacts: capacity-sim worksheet, runbook for scale-up, and a workshop recording + notes

Scope (in-scope):
- Dedicated GPU pool simulation with the customer's traffic trace (they provided a day-of-week export)
- Micro-benchmarking of batching thresholds, KV cache hit-rate impact, and cold-start scenarios for 1–3 model variants
- Short workshop with Acme engineering (2 hours) to review findings and next steps

Non-goals / out-of-scope:
- Full infra deployment in customer VPC (we will provide configs & Terraform snippets but not operate)
- Extensive model fine-tuning or data labeling work

Assumptions for capacity model (explicit):
- Arrival process: non-homogeneous Poisson with AM spike (08:00–10:00 local) multiplier x3, baseline otherwise
- Average conversation length: 3 turns, mean response tokens = 90, 15% > 512 tokens
- Batch formation latency target = 20ms for continuous batching
- KV cache hit rate scenarios: 20%, 50%, 80% (we'll simulate all three)
- Hardware candidate: 8x A100 80GB equivalent (Discrete units = 1 pool)

Week-by-week plan (3 weeks):
Week 0 (prep, pre-reqs) - 4 business days before kick:
- Collect traffic export and sample traces from Acme (OWNER: Jon Park, 1d)
- Provision sandbox Dedicated pool & baseline model image (OWNER: Infra eng, 2d)
- Confirm monitoring hooks + tracing + S3 bucket for logs (OWNER: Sofia, 1d)

Week 1 (benchmarks + initial sim) - sprint days 1–5:
- Run microbenchmarks across batching thresholds (1, 8, 16, 32) and kv-hit scenarios (OWNER: Ethan, 3d)
- Produce capacity-sim baseline (csv + short writeup) and run preliminary cost calc (OWNER: Aisha, 2d)
- Identify immediate tuning wins (hot-path kernels, kernel selection tuning) and open a runtime PR if needed (OWNER: Ethan, 2d)

Week 2 (stress tests + fallbacks) - sprint days 6–10:
- Inject real trace into pool to simulate morning burst; measure p50/p95/p99 and error profile (OWNER: Jon, 3d)
- Validate fallback variant (quantized) and measure quality delta on sample prompt set (OWNER: Sofia, 2d)
- Prepare workshop artifacts (slides, short demo script) (OWNER: Aisha, 1d)

Week 3 (workshop + handoff) - sprint days 11–15:
- Run customer-facing workshop (2h) + record (OWNER: Aisha)
- Deliver final capacity-sim worksheet, runbook, and next-step proposal doc (OWNER: Aisha + Sofia)
- Internal retro & lessons learned (OWNER: team, 1/2 day)

Task tracker (short form, includes quick ETA and status markers):
- get-traffic-export.csv (Jon Park) - ETA: day -3 - status: todo
- sandbox-provisioned.tf (Infra) - ETA: day -2 - status: in_progress
- bench-batch-thresholds.md (Ethan Kim) - ETA: week1 day3 - status: todo
- capacity-sim-v1.csv + readme (Aisha) - ETA: week1 day5 - status: todo
- fallback-quantized-eval (Sofia Martinez) - ETA: week2 day3 - status: todo
- workshop-slides.pdf (Aisha) - ETA: week2 day5 - status: draft
- runbook-scaleup.md (Sofia) - ETA: week3 day2 - status: todo

Quick sim results (toy run, put inline for visibility):
- Scenario A (20% kv-hit, batch=8): p95=410ms, p50=170ms, tokens/sec/node=1200 -> requires 3 nodes to meet p95<350ms
- Scenario B (50% kv-hit, batch=16): p95=320ms, p50=150ms, tokens/sec/node=1600 -> requires 2 nodes
- Scenario C (80% kv-hit, batch=8): p95=280ms, p50=120ms, tokens/sec/node=1900 -> requires 2 nodes
Notes: these are preliminary and assume continuous batching latency=20ms; we'll produce a proper CSV with param sweep.

Workshop agenda (2h):
- 0:00–0:10: goals + quick overview of deliverables
- 0:10–0:30: customer workload & assumptions recap (live review of trace)
- 0:30–1:00: demo: baseline Dedicated run + monitoring dashboard (p95 focus)
- 1:00–1:20: stress test replay & fallback demo (quantized variant)
- 1:20–1:40: capacity model walkthrough and cost estimate tradeoffs
- 1:40–2:00: decisions, next steps, and sign-offs

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: traffic trace not representative -> Mitigation: run additional synthetic scenarios with longer tails and heavier seq-lengths (owner: Jon)
- Risk: kernel-level perf regression found -> Mitigation: have a short rollback/fallback plan to a known-good kernel set and use model fallback path (owner: Ethan)
- Risk: customer regulatory constraints prevent Private fallback -> Mitigation: prepare documented security/attestation checklist and escalate to security (owner: Sofia)

Open questions (for kickoff):
- Can Acme provide 7-day traffic sample or only single-day? (impacts tail estimation)
- Any hard SLOs outside of the p95 latency? e.g., max error rate, throughput floor?
- Is there a preferred cost target (dollars per 1k active users)?

Next immediate steps (today / 48h):
1) Jon: confirm traffic export + timezone mapping, deliver sample by EOD +2
2) Infra: start sandbox Dedicated pool provisioning, aim for POC image by +3
3) Aisha/Sofia: draft workshop slides and list of demo prompts

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep workshop lightweight — customers get bored with too much infra detail; focus on capacity story and clear action items
- Consider adding a lightweight RL/monitoring spike to show autopilot scaling policy as an appendix if time
- TODO: drop an invite into #acct-acmecorp and pin the trace file link

Attachments we will produce:
- capacity-sim-v1.csv (param sweep), capacity-sim-readme.md, runbook-scaleup.md, workshop-slides.pdf, workshop-recording.mp4

If anyone reading this wants to add a test scenario, drop it into the linked spreadsheet or ping me directly.
